facts.statement: The genus Gallimimus was named by Osmólska and colleagues in 1972.
facts.quote: Osmólska et al., 1972

facts.statement: Fossils of Gallimimus were discovered in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia during the 1960s by Polish-Mongolian expeditions.
facts.quote: Several fossils in various stages of growth were discovered by Polish-Mongolian expeditions in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia during the 1960s

facts.statement: A large skeleton found in the Gobi Desert was designated the holotype for Gallimimus bullatus in 1972.
facts.quote: a large skeleton discovered in this region was made the holotype specimen of the new genus and species Gallimimus bullatus in 1972

facts.statement: The name Gallimimus means "chicken mimic" because its neck vertebrae resemble those of chickens.
facts.quote: The generic name means "chicken mimic", referring to the similarities between its neck vertebrae and those of the Galliformes

facts.statement: Gallimimus is the largest known member of the ornithomimid group of dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Gallimimus is the largest known ornithomimid

facts.statement: Adult Gallimimus measured about 6 meters in length, 1.9 meters in height at the hip, and weighed between 400 and 490 kilograms.
facts.quote: adults were about 6 m long, 1.9 m tall at the hip and weighed about 400 - 490 kg

facts.statement: Gallimimus was toothless, possessing a horny beak and a delicate lower jaw.
facts.quote: Gallimimus was toothless with a keratinous (horny) beak, and had a delicate lower jaw

facts.statement: Many of Gallimimus's vertebrae were pneumatic, containing air-filled openings.
facts.quote: Many of the vertebrae had openings that indicate they were pneumatic (air-filled)

facts.statement: Gallimimus had hands with three digits and curved claws, which were proportionally the shortest among ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: The hands were proportionally the shortest of any ornithomimosaur and each had three digits with curved claws

facts.statement: Gallimimus was a fast-running animal estimated to reach speeds of 42 to 56 km/h (29 to 34 mph) to escape predators.
facts.quote: As an ornithomimid, Gallimimus would have been a fleet (or cursorial) animal, using its speed to escape predators; its speed has been estimated at 42–56 km/h (29–34 mph)

facts.statement: Evidence from a bone bed suggests Gallimimus may have lived in groups.
facts.quote: Gallimimus may have lived in groups, based on the discovery of several specimens preserved in a bone bed

facts.statement: There is an ongoing debate regarding the diet of Gallimimus, with theories ranging from carnivory to herbivory and filter-feeding.
facts.quote: Various theories have been proposed regarding the diet of Gallimimus and other ornithomimids

facts.statement: It is debated whether structures in Gallimimus's beak were used for water filter-feeding or for processing tough plant material.
facts.quote: It has also been suggested that it used small columnar structures in its beak for filter-feeding in water, though these structures may instead have been ridges used for feeding on tough plant material, indicative of a herbivorous diet

facts.statement: Polish-Mongolian paleontological expeditions to the Gobi Desert were organized between 1963 and 1965.
facts.quote: Between 1963 and 1965, the Polish Academy of Sciences and the Mongolian Academy of Sciences organised the Polish-Mongolian palaeontological expeditions to the Gobi Desert of Mongolia

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Gallimimus bullatus was discovered by Zofia Kielan-Jaworowska in Tsaagan Khushuu in 1964.
facts.quote: The largest skeleton (later to become the holotype of Gallimimus bullatus) was discovered by palaeontologist Zofia Kielan-Jaworowska in Tsaagan Khushuu in 1964

facts.statement: A small Gallimimus skeleton lacking forelimbs was found in 1967 in Bugeen Tsav by a Mongolian expedition.
facts.quote: A small skeleton without forelimbs was discovered in 1967 by the Mongolian palaeontological expedition in Bugeen Tsav outside the Nemegt Basin

facts.statement: At the time of its naming, twenty-five specimens of Gallimimus were known, including nine represented only by single bones.
facts.quote: Osmólska and colleagues listed twenty-five known specimens in all, nine of which were only represented by single bones

facts.statement: Several Gallimimus specimens have been looted due to fossil poaching, a serious problem in 21st-century Mongolia.
facts.quote: Fossil poaching has become a serious problem in Mongolia in the 21st century, and several Gallimimus specimens have been looted

facts.statement: A fossil trackway associated with a clenched Gallimimus foot was reported in 2017 based on a discovery made in 2009.
facts.quote: In 2017, Hang-Jae Lee and colleagues reported a fossil trackway discovered in 2009 associated with a clenched Gallimimus foot (specimen MPC-D100F/17)

facts.statement: A slab containing two Gallimimus specimens was repatriated to Mongolia in 2014 after being smuggled to the United States.
facts.quote: In 2014, a slab with two Gallimimus specimens was repatriated to Mongolia along with other dinosaur skeletons, after having been smuggled to the US

facts.statement: Gallimimus belongs to the family Ornithomimidae, which is part of the group Ornithomimosauria.
facts.quote: The family Ornithomimidae is part of the group Ornithomimosauria

facts.statement: Based on its relative Ornithomimus, it is highly likely that Gallimimus had feathers.
facts.quote: As evidenced by its relative Ornithomimus, it is highly likely it would have had feathers

facts.statement: In 1988, Gregory S. Paul reclassified the species as Ornithomimus bullatus based on skull similarities among ornithomimids.
facts.quote: In 1988, the palaeontologist Gregory S. Paul concluded that the skulls of ornithomimids were more similar to each other than previously thought and moved most species into the same genus, Ornithomimus, resulting in the new combination O. bullatus.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul later listed the species as Gallimimus (or Struthiomimus) bullatus in 2010 before reverting to Gallimimus in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2010, he instead listed it as "Gallimimus (or Struthiomimus) bullatus", but returned to using only the genus name Gallimimus in 2016.

facts.statement: In 2000, Philip J. Currie proposed that Anserimimus was a junior synonym of Gallimimus, a claim dismissed by Kobayashi and Barsbold due to observed differences.
facts.quote: In 2000, the palaeontologist Philip J. Currie proposed that Anserimimus, which is only known from one skeleton from Mongolia, was a junior synonym of Gallimimus, but this was dismissed by Kobayashi and Barsbold, who pointed out several differences between the two.

facts.statement: Barsbold noted morphological variation among newer Gallimimus specimens, but this observation has never been published.
facts.quote: Barsbold noted some morphological variation among newer Gallimimus specimens, though this has never been published.

facts.statement: In 2006, Kobayashi and Barsbold proposed that the nearly complete skeleton IGM 100/14, informally called Gallimimus mongoliensis, likely belongs to a different genus due to specific differences.
facts.quote: Barsbold informally referred to a nearly complete skeleton (IGM 100/14) as "Gallimimus mongoliensis", but since it differs from Gallimimus in some details, Yoshitsugu Kobayashi and Barsbold proposed in 2006 that it probably belongs to a different genus.

facts.statement: The adult holotype specimen IGM 100/11 was approximately 6 meters long, 1.9 meters tall at the hip, with a 330 mm skull and a 660 mm femur.
facts.quote: The adult holotype (specimen IGM 100/11) was about 6 m long and 1.9 m tall at the hip; its skull was 330 mm long and the femur (thigh bone) was 660 mm.

facts.statement: The adult Gallimimus would have weighed between 400 and 490 kg.
facts.quote: It would have weighed about 400 - 490 kg.

facts.statement: A juvenile specimen, ZPAL MgD-I/94, measured about 2.15 meters in length, 0.79 meters in height at the hip, and weighed between 26 and 30.2 kg.
facts.quote: In comparison, one juvenile specimen (ZPAL MgD-I/94) was about 2.15 m long, 0.79 m tall at the hip, and weighed about 26 - 30.2 kg.

facts.statement: Evidence from related Ornithomimus fossils indicates that adult Gallimimus were feathered and possessed wing-like structures, shown by quill-knobs on the ulna bone.
facts.quote: Based on fossils of the related Ornithomimus, it is known that ornithomimosaurs ("ostrich dinosaurs") were feathered, and that the adults bore wing-like structures as evidenced by the presence of quill-knobs on the ulna bone of the lower arm, bumps that indicate where feathers would have attached.

facts.statement: Gallimimus had a long skull compared to other ornithomimids due to its snout length, featuring a gently convex sloping upper profile.
facts.quote: Due to the length of its snout, the skull was long compared to other ornithomimids, and the snout had a gently convex sloping upper profile.

facts.statement: Viewed from above, the Gallimimus snout was almost spatulate, broad, and rounded at the tip, contrasting with the acute, V-shaped snouts of North American ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Seen from above, the snout was almost spatulate (spoon-shaped), broad and rounded at the tip (or U-shaped), whereas it was acute (or V-shaped) in North American ornithomimids.

facts.statement: The orbits of Gallimimus were large and faced sideways, similar to other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: The orbits (eye sockets) were large and faced sideways, as in other ornithomimids.

facts.statement: The delicate lower jaw of Gallimimus consisted of thin bones, being slender and shallow at the front and deepening towards the rear.
facts.quote: The delicate lower jaw, consisting of thin bones, was slender and shallow at the front, deepening towards the rear.

facts.statement: The front of the Gallimimus mandible was shovel-like, creating a gap between the jaw tips when shut.
facts.quote: The front of the mandible was shovel-like, resulting in a gap between the tips of the jaws when shut.

facts.statement: The jaws of Gallimimus were toothless, with the front part covered in a keratinous rhamphotheca, or horny beak, during life.
facts.quote: The jaws of Gallimimus were edentulous (toothless), and the front part would have been covered in a keratinous rhamphotheca (horny beak) in life.

facts.statement: Gallimimus possessed 64 to 66 vertebrae in its spine, a count lower than that of other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Gallimimus had 64–66 vertebrae in its spine, fewer than other ornithomimids.

facts.statement: Gallimimus had a neck that was proportionally longer relative to its trunk compared to other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: The neck appears to have been proportionally longer in relation to the trunk than in other ornithomimids.

facts.statement: The sacrum of Gallimimus was composed of five sacral vertebrae of approximately equal length.
facts.quote: The sacrum (fused vertebrae between the pelvic bones) consisted of five sacral vertebrae which were about equal in length.

facts.statement: Gallimimus had three similarly developed fingers where the first was the strongest, the third the weakest, and the second the longest.
facts.quote: It had three fingers, which were similarly developed; the first (the "thumb") was the strongest, the third was the weakest and the second was the longest.

facts.statement: Gallimimus possessed an arctometatarsalian foot structure where the lower half of the third metatarsal wedged between the other two, narrowing abruptly at mid-length.
facts.quote: The lower half of the third metatarsal was broad when viewed end on, partly covering the adjoining two metatarsals to each side, but narrowed abruptly at mid-length, wedging between those bones and disappearing (an arctometatarsalian foot structure).

facts.statement: Like other ornithomimids, Gallimimus lacked a hallux, or dewclaw, on its foot.
facts.quote: As in other ornithomimids, the foot had no hallux (or dewclaw, the first toe of most other theropods).

facts.statement: In 1976, Barsbold established the new group Ornithomimosauria to contain the family Ornithomimidae.
facts.quote: In 1976, Barsbold placed Ornithomimidae in the new group Ornithomimosauria.

facts.statement: Gallimimus belonged to the clade Maniraptoriformes within coelurosaurian theropods, a group that also includes modern birds.
facts.quote: Ornithomimosaurs belonged to the clade Maniraptoriformes of coelurosaurian theropods, which also includes modern birds.

facts.statement: After the separation of Europe from Asia by the Turgai Strait, ornithomimosaurs like Gallimimus were largely restricted to Asia and North America.
facts.quote: As seen in some other dinosaur groups, ornithomimosaurs were largely restricted to Asia and North America after Europe was separated from Asia by the Turgai Strait.

facts.statement: In 1994, Thomas R. Holtz named the clade Bullatosauria, which included ornithomimosaurs and troodontids, based on the specific name Gallimimus bullatus and a shared bulbous capsule on the parasphenoid.
facts.quote: In 1994, the palaeontologist Thomas R. Holtz grouped ornithomimosaurs and troodontids in a clade, based on shared features such as the presence of a bulbous capsule on the parasphenoid. He named the clade Bullatosauria, based on the specific name of Gallimimus bullatus, which was also in reference to the capsule.

facts.statement: Gallimimus held its neck at an oblique angle of 35 degrees.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebrae of Gallimimus indicate that it held its neck obliquely, declining upwards at an angle of 35 degrees.

facts.statement: Gallimimus had non-prehensile hands with a non-opposable thumb.
facts.quote: Osmólska and colleagues found that the hands of Gallimimus were not prehensile (or capable of grasping), and that the thumb was not opposable.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested Gallimimus had weak arms compared to other ornithomimosaurs like Deinocheirus.
facts.quote: They also suggested that the arms were weak compared to, for example, those of the ornithomimosaur Deinocheirus.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Dale Russell suggested in 1972 that Gallimimus was a fast, cursorial animal that used speed to escape predators.
facts.quote: They agreed with the interpretations of ornithomimid biology by palaeontologist Dale Russell from earlier in 1972, including that they would have been very fleet (or cursorial) animals, although less agile than large, modern ground birds, and would have used their speed to escape predators.

facts.statement: Dale Russell suggested Gallimimus possessed vision and intelligence comparable to modern ratite birds.
facts.quote: Russell also suggested that they had a good sense of vision and intelligence comparable to that of modern ratite birds.

facts.statement: Richard A. Thulborn estimated in 1982 that Gallimimus could run at speeds between 42 and 56 km/h.
facts.quote: In 1982, palaeontologist Richard A. Thulborn estimated that Gallimimus could have run at speeds of 42–56 km/h (29–34 mph).

facts.statement: Thulborn noted that Gallimimus was likely slower than ostriches (70–80 km/h) because its arms and tail added weight.
facts.quote: He found that ornithomimids would not have been as fast as ostriches, which can reach 70–80 km/h (43–49 mph), in part due to their arms and tails increasing their weight.

facts.statement: Paul suggested in 1988 that Gallimimus had flattened eyeballs with minimal mobility, requiring head movement to see.
facts.quote: In 1988, Paul suggested that the eyeballs of ornithomimids were flattened and had minimal mobility within the sockets, necessitating movement of the head to view objects.

facts.statement: Paul suggested Gallimimus's sideways-facing eyes provided limited binocular vision but improved the ability to see predators behind them.
facts.quote: Since their eyes faced more sideways than in some other bird-like theropods, their binocular vision would have been more limited, which is an adaptation in some animals that improves their ability to see predators behind them.

facts.statement: Paul considered Gallimimus's short tails and missing halluxes to be adaptations for speed.
facts.quote: Paul considered the relatively short tails, which reduced weight, and missing halluxes of ornithomimids to be adaptations for speed.

facts.statement: Paul suggested Gallimimus could defend itself by pecking and kicking but mainly relied on speed to escape.
facts.quote: He suggested that they could have defended themselves by pecking and kicking, but would have mainly relied on their speed for escape.

facts.statement: Akinobu Watanabe and colleagues found in 2015 that Gallimimus had the most pneumatized skeleton among ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: In 2015, Akinobu Watanabe and colleagues found that together with Deinocheirus and Archaeornithomimus, Gallimimus had the most pneumatised skeleton among ornithomimosaurs.

facts.statement: The function of pneumatization in Gallimimus is debated, with hypotheses including mass reduction, high metabolism, balance, or thermoregulation.
facts.quote: Pneumatisation is thought to be advantageous for flight in modern birds, but its function in non-avian dinosaurs is not known with certainty.

facts.statement: The simultaneous death of Gallimimus individuals suggests they may have lived in groups.
facts.quote: The fact that the animals seem to have died at the same time (the empty excavation pits were stratigraphically identical) may indicate that Gallimimus was gregarious (lived in groups), which has also been suggested for other ornithomimids.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Gallimimus had a highly mobile front neck and rigid hind neck, similar to chickens, which likely aided in locating ground prey.
facts.quote: Osmólska and colleagues pointed out that the front part of the neck of Gallimimus would have been very mobile (the hind part was more rigid), the neural arches in the vertebrae of that region being similar to chicken and other Galliformes, indicating similar feeding habits.

facts.statement: The beak of Gallimimus resembled that of a duck or goose, and it likely swallowed small living prey whole.
facts.quote: They found the beak of Gallimimus similar to that of a duck or goose, and that it would have fed on small, living prey which it swallowed whole.

facts.statement: Paleontologists assumed all ornithomimids shared similar feeding habits, comparing their beaks to those of insectivorous birds.
facts.quote: They assumed that all ornithomimids had similar feeding habits, and pointed out that Russel had compared the beaks of ornithomimids with those of insectivorous birds.

facts.statement: Osmólska and colleagues proposed that Gallimimus could perform cranial kinesis, allowing skull bones to move relative to each other.
facts.quote: Osmólska and colleagues suggested that Gallimimus was capable of cranial kinesis (due to the seemingly loose connection between some of the bones at the back of the skull), a feature which allows individual bones of the skull to move in relation to each other.

facts.statement: Researchers proposed Gallimimus used its short forelimbs for raking or digging to access food rather than bringing food to its mouth.
facts.quote: They also proposed that it did not use its short handed forelimbs for bringing food to the mouth, but for raking or digging in the ground to access food.

facts.statement: In 2001, Norell, Makovicky, and Currie reported a Gallimimus skull (IGM 100/1133) preserving soft tissue structures on the beak.
facts.quote: In 2001, palaeontologists Mark A. Norell, Makovicky, and Currie reported a Gallimimus skull (IGM 100/1133) and an Ornithomimus skull that preserved soft tissue structures on the beak.

facts.statement: Columnar structures inside the Gallimimus beak were similar to lamellae in anseriform birds, used for manipulating food, filter-feeding, and cutting plants.
facts.quote: The inner side of the Gallimimus beak had columnar structures that the authors found similar to the lamellae in the beaks of anseriform birds, which use these for manipulating food, straining sediments, filter-feeding by segregating food items from other material, and for cutting plants while grazing.

facts.statement: In 2005, Paul Barrett argued that Gallimimus beak structures were likely rigid ridges like those in turtles and hadrosaurs rather than flexible filter-feeding bristles.
facts.quote: In 2005, palaeontologist Paul Barrett pointed out that the lamella-like structures of Gallimimus did not appear to have been flexible bristles like those of filter-feeding birds (as there is no indication of these structures overlapping or being collapsed), but were instead more akin to the thin, regularly spaced vertical ridges in the beaks of turtles and hadrosaurid dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Barrett suggested the beak ridges indicated Gallimimus was a herbivore feeding on high-fibre material.
facts.quote: Barrett suggested that the ridges in the beak of Gallimimus represented a natural cast of the internal surface of the beak, indicating that the animal was a herbivore that fed on material high in fibre.

facts.statement: In 2007, Espen M. Knutsen noted ornithomimid beak shapes were consistent with omnivory or high-fibre herbivory.
facts.quote: In 2007, palaeontologist Espen M. Knutsen wrote that the beak shape of ornithomimids, when compared to those of modern birds, was consistent with omnivory or high-fibre herbivory.

facts.statement: In 2019, Button and Zanno found herbivorous dinosaurs fed either by gut processing (gracile skulls, low bite force) or mouth processing (extensive processing features).
facts.quote: David J. Button and Zanno found in 2019 herbivorous dinosaurs mainly followed two distinct modes of feeding, either processing food in the gut—characterized by gracile skulls and low bite forces—or the mouth, characterized by features associated with extensive processing.

facts.statement: Button and Zanno suggested Gallimimus and deinocheirids separately invaded herbivorous niches, convergently achieving large sizes.
facts.quote: These researchers suggested that ornithomimid ornithomimosaurians such as Gallimimus and deinocheirids had invaded these niches separately, convergently achieving relatively large sizes.

facts.statement: Gallimimus skulls changed during growth, with the rear and orbits shrinking while the snout lengthened, similar to modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: The shape and proportions of the skull changed significantly during growth. The rear of the skull and the orbits decreased in size, whereas the snout became relatively longer; similar changes occur in modern crocodiles.

facts.statement: In 2012, Zelenitsky and colleagues concluded adult ornithomimosaur arm structures were likely secondary sexual characteristics used for courtship, display, or brooding.
facts.quote: In 2012, palaeontologist Darla K. Zelenitsky and colleagues concluded that, since adult ornithomimosaurs had wing-like structures on their arms whereas juveniles did not (as evidenced by specimens of Ornithomimus), these structures were originally secondary sexual characteristics, which could have been used for reproductive behaviour such as courtship, display, and brooding.

facts.statement: In 1987, Pawlicki and Bolechała found age-related differences in calcium and phosphorus content in Gallimimus bones.
facts.quote: A 1987 study by the biologists Roman Pawlicki and P. Bolechała showed age-related differences in the content of calcium and phosphorus (important components in the formation of bone) of Gallimimus specimens.

facts.statement: In 1991, Pawlicki and Bolechała reported older Gallimimus individuals had higher lead and iron levels in their bones than younger ones.
facts.quote: In 1991, they reported that the bones of old individuals contained the highest amounts of lead and iron, while those in younger animals were lower.

facts.statement: In 2000, Rensberger and Watabe found Gallimimus bone histology resembled birds more than mammals, unlike ornithischian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: A study of the bone histology of various dinosaurs in 2000, by biologists John M. Rensberger and Mahito Watabe, revealed that the canaliculi (channels which connect bone cells) and collagen fibre bundles of Gallimimus and other ornithomimids were more akin to those in birds than mammals, unlike those of ornithischian dinosaurs, which were more similar to mammals.

facts.statement: Gallimimus lived about 70 million years ago during the early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: This geologic formation has never been dated radiometrically, but the fauna present in the fossil record indicate it was probably deposited during the early Maastrichtian stage, at the end of the Late Cretaceous about 70 million years ago.

facts.statement: Gallimimus fossils have been found in the Nemegt Formation in the Gobi Desert of southern Mongolia.
facts.quote: Gallimimus is known from the Nemegt Formation in the Gobi Desert of southern Mongolia.

facts.statement: The habitat of Gallimimus experienced a humid climate with periodic droughts, evidenced by river channels and caliche deposits.
facts.quote: Large river channels and soil deposits are evidence of a significantly more humid climate than those found in the older Barun Goyot and Djadochta formations, although caliche deposits indicate that periodic droughts occurred.

facts.statement: Gallimimus was adapted for running due to its light build and long hind legs.
facts.quote: Debido a su constitución ligera y sus largas patas traseras, este dinosaurio estaba adaptado para la carrera.

facts.statement: Gallimimus resembled an ostrich with a long neck and a toothless beak.
facts.quote: Su aspecto recuerda al de un avestruz dado su largo cuello y su pico sin dientes.

facts.statement: Gallimimus used its long tail to maintain balance while moving.
facts.quote: Su larga cola le servía para mantener el equilibrio al avanzar.

facts.statement: The genus Gallimimus was described by Osmólska, Roniewics, and Barsbold in 1972.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Osmólska, Roniewics & Barsbold, 1972

facts.statement: The type locality for Gallimimus is the Nemegt Formation in Mongolia.
facts.quote: Fue hallado en la Formación Nemegt, en Mongolia.

facts.statement: Gallimimus is classified within the infraorder Ornithomimosauria.
facts.quote: infraordo: Ornithomimosauria

facts.statement: Gallimimus belongs to the family Ornithomimidae.
facts.quote: familia: Ornithomimidae

facts.statement: The species Gallimimus bullatus is the only known species in the genus Gallimimus.
facts.quote: genus: Gallimimus

facts.statement: Gallimimus was featured in the 1993 movie Jurassic Park directed by Steven Spielberg.
facts.quote: Gallimimus was featured in the 1993 movie Jurassic Park by director Steven Spielberg

facts.statement: The Gallimimus in Jurassic Park were animated using footage of ostriches and herding gazelles as references.
facts.quote: The Gallimimus were animated by tracing frames from footage of ostriches, and footage of herding gazelles was also referenced.

facts.statement: It has been claimed that the Lark Quarry tracks in Queensland, Australia, inspired the Gallimimus stampede scene in Jurassic Park, though this is contested.
facts.quote: It has been claimed that the Lark Quarry tracks (one of the world's largest concentrations of dinosaur tracks) in Queensland, Australia, served as inspiration and "scientific underpinning" for the Gallimimus stampede scene in Jurassic Park

facts.statement: Gallimimus was the most common ornithomimosaur found in the Nemegt Formation.
facts.quote: Gallimimus is the most common member of the group in the Nemegt.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the Lark Quarry tracks represent a dinosaur stampede caused by a theropod or a herbivore, and whether they inspired the Jurassic Park scene.
facts.quote: The idea that the tracks represent a stampede has since been contested (the "theropod" may instead have been a herbivore similar to Muttaburrasaurus), and a consultant to Jurassic Park has denied the tracks served as inspiration for the movie.

facts.statement: Gallimimus is the largest known member of the family Ornithomimidae.
facts.quote: Gallimimus es el miembro más grande conocido de la familia Ornithomimidae.

facts.statement: The adult holotype specimen was approximately 6 meters long and 1.9 meters tall at the hip.
facts.quote: El holotipo adulto, espécimen IGM 100/11, tenía aproximadamente 6 metros de largo y 1,9 metros de altura en la cadera.

facts.statement: The adult holotype would have weighed approximately 440 kilograms.
facts.quote: Habría pesado unos 440 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Based on relative fossils, ornithomimids had feathers and adults carried wing-like structures, evidenced by knobs on the ulna indicating where feathers attached.
facts.quote: Sobre la base de los fósiles de los parientes Ornithomimus, se sabe que los ornitomímidos tenían plumas y los adultos portaban estructuras en forma de alas, como lo demuestra la presencia de perillas en el hueso del cúbito de la parte inferior del brazo, protuberancias que indican dónde se habrían adherido las plumas.

facts.statement: Gallimimus resembled modern ostriches with a small head, large eyes, long neck, small forelimbs, strong running legs, and a long tail.
facts.quote: Gallimimus era en apariencia similar a los actuales avestruces, cabeza pequeña, grandes ojos, cuello largo, miembros anteriores pequeños, fuertes patas para correr y una larga cola.

facts.statement: A diagnostic feature of Gallimimus is its short hands compared to the humerus when compared to other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Un carácter de diagnóstico de Gallimimus son sus manos cortas en comparación al húmero, cuando se lo compara con otros ornitomímidos.

facts.statement: Its forelimbs were relatively short compared to the hind limbs and ended with three claws on each hand.
facts.quote: Sus patas delanteras eran relativamente cortas comparadas con las traseras, y estaban rematados con tres garras en cada mano.

facts.statement: Some experts suggest the claws may have been used to dig in the earth to obtain eggs, roots, and tubers for food.
facts.quote: Algunos expertos han dado utilidad a las garras del Gallimimus aventurando que pudieron servirle para escarbar en la tierra y conseguir así huevos, raíces y tubérculos con los que alimentarse.

facts.statement: The tail was used as a counterbalance.
facts.quote: La cola era utilizada como contrapeso.

facts.statement: The eyes were located on the sides of its head, meaning it did not possess binocular vision.
facts.quote: Los ojos estaban situados a los lados de su cabeza, significando que no poseía la visión binocular.

facts.statement: Like most modern birds, it had hollow bones.
facts.quote: Como la mayoría de los pájaros modernos, tenía huesos huecos.

facts.statement: Gallimimus had adaptations suggesting good running ability, including long limbs, a long tibia and metatarsus, and short foot digits.
facts.quote: Gallimimus tenía un número de adaptaciones que sugieren buena capacidad para correr, miembros largos, con una tibia y metatarso largos y los dedos del pie cortos.

facts.statement: A fossilized beak present in a Gallimimus skull was bordered by a beak interpreted as part of a filtering mechanism like that of ducks.
facts.quote: Un pico fosilizado presente en un cráneo de Gallimimus estaba bordeado de un pico que se ha interpretado como parte de un mecanismo de filtrado como los de los patos.

facts.statement: It is more probable that Gallimimus was an omnivore, using its beak for plants and capturing small animals.
facts.quote: Parece más probable que Gallimimus fuese un omnívoro, usando su pico en las plantas y la captura de pequeños animales.

facts.statement: Speculation on its diet suggests it may have fed on insects and small worms, complementing its insectivorous diet with some plants and eggs.
facts.quote: Sobre el Gallimimus se ha especulado sobre su dieta, sugiriendo que pudo haberse alimentado de insectos y de pequeños gusanos y pudo complementar su dieta insectívora con algunas plantas y huevos.

facts.statement: The head of Gallimimus was very small and light compared to the vertebral column.
facts.quote: La cabeza de Gallimimus era muy pequeña y ligera en comparación con la columna vertebral.

facts.statement: Due to the length of its snout, the skull was long compared to other ornithomimids and the snout had a slightly inclined upper profile.
facts.quote: Debido a la longitud de su hocico, el cráneo era largo comparado con otros ornitomímidos y el hocico tenía un perfil superior ligeramente inclinado.

facts.statement: Viewed from above, the snout was almost spatulate, spoon-shaped, wide and rounded at the tip in a U-shape, whereas it was acute or V-shaped in North American ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Visto desde arriba, el hocico era casi espatulado, en forma de cuchara, ancho y redondeado en la punta , en forma de U, mientras que era agudo o en forma de V en los ornitomímidos norteamericanos.

facts.statement: The eye sockets were large and oriented to the sides, as in other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Las cuencas de los ojos eran grandes y estaban orientadas hacia los lados, como en otros ornitomímidos.

facts.statement: The delicate lower jaw, formed by thin bones, was thin and shallow in the front, deepening towards the back.
facts.quote: La delicada mandíbula inferior, formada por huesos delgados, era delgada y poco profunda en la parte delantera, profundizándose hacia la parte posterior.

facts.statement: The front of the jaw was shovel-shaped, resulting in a gap between the jaw tips when closed.
facts.quote: La parte frontal de la mandíbula tenía forma de pala, lo que resultaba en un espacio entre las puntas de las mandíbulas cuando se cerraba.

facts.statement: The jaws of Gallimimus were toothless, without teeth, and the front would have been covered by a horny beak in life.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas de Gallimimus estaban desdentadas, sin dientes y la parte frontal se habría cubierto de un pico córneo en vida.

facts.statement: The inner side of the beak had small, tight, uniformly spaced columnar structures, the exact nature of which is debated, being longer in the front and shortened towards the back.
facts.quote: El lado interno del pico tenía estructuras columnares pequeñas, apretadas y espaciadas uniformemente, se discute su naturaleza exacta, que eran más largas en la parte delantera y acortadas hacia la parte posterior.

facts.statement: In comparison, a juvenile specimen was approximately 2.15 meters long, 0.79 meters tall at the hip, and weighed around 26 kilograms.
facts.quote: En comparación, un espécimen juvenil, ZPAL MgD-I / 94 tenía aproximadamente 2,15 metros de largo, 0,79 metros de altura en la cadera y pesaba alrededor de 26 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Its skull was 330 millimeters long and the femur, thigh bone, was 660 millimeters long.
facts.quote: Su cráneo tenía 330 milímetros de largo y el fémur, hueso del muslo, tenía 660 milímetros.

facts.statement: In the Mongolian form, the dorsal neural arches of the sacral vertebrae do not fuse completely even in mature specimens, in contrast to those observed in Ornithomimus and Struthiomimus.
facts.quote: en la forma mongol los arcos neurales dorsales de las vértebras sacras no se funden totalmente incluso en especímenes maduros, en contraste con esos observados en Ornithomimus y Struthiomimus.

facts.statement: Gallimimus had 64 to 66 vertebrae in its spine, which is fewer than other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Gallimimus tenía 64–66 vértebras en su columna vertebral , menos que otros ornitomímidos.

facts.statement: Many of Gallimimus's vertebrae had pneumatic foramina, suggesting they were invaded by air sacs.
facts.quote: Muchos de los centros tenían forámenes, aberturas que también se han llamado pleurocoelos y, por lo tanto, probablemente eran neumáticas, con sus cámaras huecas invadidas por sacos de aire.

facts.statement: Gallimimus's neck consisted of 10 long and wide cervical vertebrae, except for the atlas.
facts.quote: El cuello consistía en 10 vértebras cervicales, todas largas y anchas, excepto el atlas, la primera vértebra que se conecta con la parte posterior del cráneo.

facts.statement: Gallimimus's neck was proportionally longer relative to its trunk than in other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: El cuello parece haber sido proporcionalmente más largo en relación con el tronco que en otros ornitomímidos.

facts.statement: Gallimimus had 13 dorsal vertebrae with short, reel-shaped centers that became deeper and longer toward the rear.
facts.quote: La espalda de Gallimimus tenía 13 vértebras dorsales, con centros en forma de carrete que eran cortos, pero tendían a ser más profundos y más largos hacia la espalda.

facts.statement: Gallimimus's sacrum consisted of five sacral vertebrae of approximately equal length.
facts.quote: El sacro, las vértebras fusionadas entre los huesos de la pelvis, consistía en cinco vértebras sacras que eran aproximadamente iguales en longitud.

facts.statement: Gallimimus's tail had 36 to 39 caudal vertebrae, with reel-shaped centers at the front and nearly triangular, elongated ones at the back.
facts.quote: La cola tenía 36–39 vértebras caudales, con los centros de los de la parte frontal en forma de carrete, mientras que las de la parte posterior eran casi triangulares y alargados.

facts.statement: The neural spines on Gallimimus's tail were high and flat but decreased in size toward the rear, forming a crest.
facts.quote: Las espinas neurales aquí eran altas y planas, pero disminuían hacia atrás, donde se hacían como una cresta.

facts.statement: Gallimimus's scapula was short, curved, thin at the front, and thick at the back.
facts.quote: La escápula era corta y curvada, delgada en la parte delantera y gruesa en la parte posterior.

facts.statement: Gallimimus's humerus was long, twisted, and had an almost circular cross-section.
facts.quote: El húmero, el hueso del brazo superior, que tenía una sección transversal casi circular, era largo y retorcido.

facts.statement: Gallimimus's deltopectoral crest on the humerus was comparatively small, providing little surface area for attaching upper arm muscles.
facts.quote: La cresta deltopectoral en la parte frontal superior del húmero era comparativamente pequeña y, por lo tanto, proporcionaba poca superficie para unir los músculos de la parte superior del brazo.

facts.statement: Gallimimus had three fingers that developed similarly; the first (thumb) was the strongest, the third the weakest, and the second the longest.
facts.quote: Tenía tres dedos, que se desarrollaron de manera similar; el primero' el "pulgar", fue el más fuerte, el tercero fue el más débil y el segundo fue el más largo.

facts.statement: Gallimimus's claw bones were strong and slightly curved, with the first claw being more curved and laterally compressed with a deep groove on each side.
facts.quote: Los unguales, los huesos de garras, eran fuertes, algo curvados, el del primer dedo era más curvo y comprimidos lateralmente con un surco profundo en cada lado.

facts.statement: The ratio of forearm to arm in Gallimimus reached 66%, whereas in American forms it varied from 70% to as high as 91% in Dromiceiomimus.
facts.quote: El cociente del antebrazo con el brazo alcanza el 66% en Gallimimus, mientras que en las formas americanas varía del 70% a incluso el 91% en Dromiceiomimus.

facts.statement: In Gallimimus, the ratio of dorsal to caudal vertebrae was 85%, which is higher than in other genera like Struthiomimus, where it is approximately 76%.
facts.quote: En Gallimimus el cociente de las vértebras dorsales con las caudales del 85% es mayor que en otros géneros, en Struthiomimus, por ejemplo, este cociente es el aproximadamente 76%.

facts.statement: Gallimimus belongs to the parent group Ornithomimidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ornithomimidae

facts.statement: Gallimimus is classified in the family Ornithomimidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ornithomimidae

facts.statement: Gallimimus is classified under the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Gallimimus lived from the Turonian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 93.9 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Maastrichtian (93.9 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 30 recorded fossil occurrences of Gallimimus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 30
